description: Planetary longitude time series: planet degrees seen from the Earth and from the Sun (geocentric and heliocentric) at a moment or every hour to every week, as pandas-ready columns, with speeds, retrograde flags and declinations. E.g. {start: '2024-01-01', end: '2024-12-31', interval: '1w', bodies: ['jupiter', 'saturn']}. Planetary longitudes as data: at a moment, or as a series of up to 1000 samples (columns ready for pandas). Geocentric apparent and heliocentric geometric, each with its speed and retrograde flag; optional offsets (longitude + angle), circular or arithmetic multi-body averages, unwrapped degrees for plotting, and declinations. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.20 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/longitude-series (x402 or MPP); always paid, never a free call.

average_method.description: 'arithmetic' mean of the 0-360 longitude values or 'circular' (vector) mean of the directions.

averages.description: Multi-body longitude averages: mean_of_5 = (Jupiter+Saturn+Uranus+Neptune+Pluto)/5, circle_of_8 = (Mercury+Venus+Mars+Jupiter+Saturn+Uranus+Neptune+Pluto)/8, in each perspective.

bodies.description: Bodies. Default: Sun..Pluto (geocentric), Mercury..Pluto with the Earth (heliocentric).

datetime.description: A moment (snapshot): ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00Z'. A local time needs 'timezone' or coordinates. Omit when giving start/end.

end.description: Series: last UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 1000 samples).

format.description: Series layout: 'columns' (pandas.DataFrame(result['series'])) or 'rows' (one object per sample).

include_declination.description: Series: also a declination column per body.

interval.description: Series sampling step: 1 hour, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 day or 1 week.

offsets.description: Angles in degrees added to every longitude (+angle and -angle), 'all' or a list from [0, 30, 45, 60, 72, 90, 120, 135, 144, 150, 180]. Default: none (the longitude itself).

perspective.description: Geocentric, heliocentric, or both in one call (default).

start.description: Series: first UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD. Example: '2024-01-01'.

time_utc.description: Series: UTC time of day of the first sample, HH:MM.

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates, with the historical offset (DST, Local Mean Time) of that date.

unwrap.description: Series: continuous degrees (no 360 -> 0 jump), for plotting.

name: longitude_series

accepts.description: x402 offer only: the payment options (scheme, network, amount, asset, payTo, ...).

endpoint.description: The REST route that computed it, e.g. 'astronomy/rise-set'.

error.description: x402 offer only: why payment is required.

deterministic.description: Always true: same input, same result.

llm_used.description: Always false: no language model is involved.

payment.description: How this call was paid: protocol ('free' or 'none'), price and the free calls remaining.

reproducibility.description: How to reproduce and check this result.

result_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical 'result'; check it with verify_result_hash.

resource.description: x402 offer only: the resource being paid for.

counts.description: Number of lines (snapshot) or of samples and columns (series).

lines.description: Snapshot only: one entry per line (id such as 'helio.jupiter+90', perspective, base body or average, offset, degree 0-360; speed, retrograde flag and declination on base lines).

series.description: Series only: 'columns' format = {time_utc: [...], timestamp: [...], <line id>: [...]}; 'rows' format = one object per sample.

settings.description: Settings applied: perspectives, bodies, offsets, averages and their members, frames, line id format and, for a series, interval, samples and columns.

subject.description: Snapshot only: the resolved moment (UTC, Julian days, Delta T).

warnings.description: Notes on the input or the calculation (for example an assumed local noon when only a date is given). Present only when there is something to say.

title: Planetary longitude series (geocentric + heliocentric)
